evals.name: knows the coding agent data files and their schemas
evals.prompt: In the GitHub Copilot Coding Agent environment for this repository, what pre-downloaded usage data files may exist in the workspace root, what date range does each cover, which session log file formats can appear, and how would you count interactions and detect the model used from them?
evals.expected_output: The response names ./session-logs/ (raw session log files from several editors, last 7 days, organized by datasetId/machineId/date, in both .json and .jsonl format, with .jsonl the majority) and ./usage-data/usage-agg-daily.json (aggregated daily usage from Azure Table Storage, last 30 days). For whole-document .json Copilot Chat sessions it reads requests.length for interactions and requests[].result.metadata.modelId for the model. For .jsonl sessions it identifies the editor via ./session-logs/.editor-types.json and uses that editor's schema in docs/logFilesSchema/ or the shared src/ parsers rather than the requests[] paths.
assertions: The output mentions the ./session-logs/ directory containing raw session log files covering roughly the last 7 days.
The output says session log files can be either .json or .jsonl (or that both formats must be searched), not only .json.
The output mentions ./usage-data/usage-agg-daily.json containing aggregated daily usage data covering roughly the last 30 days.

The output limits requests[].result.metadata.modelId (or equivalent path) as the model field, and the length of the requests array as the interaction count, to whole-document .json Copilot Chat sessions.

The output directs .jsonl analysis to the editor-specific schema (via ./session-logs/.editor-types.json and/or docs/logFilesSchema/) or the shared src/ parsers, instead of applying the requests[] paths to .jsonl files.
The output notes these files only exist when Azure Storage is configured for the environment (they may be absent).
